name: Ella Montoya
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember the first receipt written after a whole street closed.” Monday often includes a stop at the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms, where Ella prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
voice: I wrote down every price on the lid. Together they tell you the year the whole street went broke.
appearance: Ella is easy to recognize by a long plait tucked inside the collar and an aquiline nose and a square chin. Usually dressed in an old plum windbreaker with a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring, Ella raises one eyebrow long before saying yes when listening.
personality: Ella finds names easy and faces hard on a crowded street. People who assume they have been snubbed usually get a warmer greeting once they speak.
agenda: To date the shop's difficult winter from the price notes.
family: Ari Lane is Ella’s cousin raised in the same household. Ella leaves the first voice message. Ari calls back when there is finally a little privacy. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *A civilian apology*, Ari says, “I remember the shopkeeper's child doing sums behind the counter.”
connections: Thomas Banks. The lid that interested a collector becomes a record of a street going broke.

reactions.situation: Someone begins blaming the youngest worker for a missing item
reactions.response: Ella says what they know in their own name and refuses to treat a guess as something the child has to disprove.
